new_packages.label: שִׂיחָה וְדֶרֶךְ חָדָשׁ — תְּפִלָּה חֲדָשָׁה
new_packages.label_en: Personal Prayer and the New Path — the Fresh Prayer
new_packages.reason: These three concepts share the same essential quality: חַדְשׁוּת (novelty/freshness) — the quality of being unknown to the adversarial forces and therefore unambushable. The hitbodedut prayer (שִׂיחָה בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ), the new path (דֶּרֶךְ חָדָשׁ), and the fresh prayer (תְּפִלָּה חֲדָשָׁה) are not cause-and-effect; they are three expressions of the same thing. The Rebbe explicitly identifies them in one clause: 'הוּא דֶּרֶךְ חָדָשׁ וּתְפִלָּה חֲדָשָׁה'. All three share the nature: spoken fresh from the heart, unknown to the destructive forces, not yet mapped by adversarial ambush.
new_packages.source_evidence: הַשִּׂיחָה שֶׁמְּדַבֵּר הָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ, הוּא דֶּרֶךְ חָדָשׁ וּתְפִלָּה חֲדָשָׁה, שֶׁהָאָדָם אוֹמְרָהּ מִלִּבּוֹ מֵחָדָשׁ
new_packages.good_evil_mirror: This package is the good pole. Its evil mirror is Package 3 (מְחַבְּלִים וּמְקַטְרְגִים) — the adversarial forces that specifically target the known, predictable paths. Package 2 (דֶּרֶךְ כְּבוּשָׁה / תְּפִלּוֹת סְדוּרוֹת) is the vulnerable middle-domain that the evil forces exploit and that the good practice transcends.

new_packages.label: דֶּרֶךְ כְּבוּשָׁה וּתְפִלּוֹת סְדוּרוֹת
new_packages.label_en: The Beaten Path and the Set Prayers
new_packages.reason: The well-trodden road and the fixed/set prayers share the essential quality of being known (יְדוּעִים/סְדוּרִים): they are public, predictable, and therefore exploitable by adversarial forces. They are not evil in themselves — the Rebbe explicitly endorses the set prayers in line 4 and cautions not to abandon them — but in this teaching's structural argument, their knowability is the quality that makes them vulnerable. The mashal-nimshal structure equates them: the beaten road IS what the set prayers are — both are the 'mapped territory' that the ambushers know. Polarity is neutral because the set prayers and the well-known road are legitimate, even virtuous, objects/practices; they are not intrinsically aligned with evil.
new_packages.source_evidence: עַל תְּפִלּוֹת וּתְחִנּוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת הַסְּדוּרוֹת מִכְּבָר, כְּבָר יוֹדְעִין מֵהֶם כָּל הַמְחַבְּלִים וְהַמְקַטְרְגִים ... עַל הַדֶּרֶךְ הַכְּבוּשָׁה, הַיָּדוּעַ וּמְפֻרְסָם לַכֹּל, שָׁם אוֹרְבִים רוֹצְחִים וְגַזְלָנִים תָּמִיד

new_packages.label: מְחַבְּלִים וּמְקַטְרְגִים — רוֹצְחִים וְגַזְלָנִים
new_packages.label_en: Destructive Forces and Accusers — Murderers and Robbers
new_packages.reason: The destructive forces/accusers (מְחַבְּלִים וּמְקַטְרְגִים) and the murderers/robbers (רוֹצְחִים וְגַזְלָנִים) are the mashal-nimshal pair of this teaching's evil domain. They share the same essential nature: lying in ambush (אֲרִיבָה) on known pathways to intercept and harm. The robbers are not the cause of the accusers — they are two expressions of the same adversarial quality, each in their own domain (physical vs. spiritual). The mashal-nimshal structure (כְּמוֹ...כְּמוֹ כֵן) creates a direct bechina-type equivalence between them.
new_packages.source_evidence: כְּבָר יוֹדְעִין מֵהֶם כָּל הַמְחַבְּלִים וְהַמְקַטְרְגִים, וְהֵם אוֹרְבִים עַל הַדְּרָכִים ... שָׁם אוֹרְבִים רוֹצְחִים וְגַזְלָנִים תָּמִיד
new_packages.good_evil_mirror: This package is the evil pole, mirroring Package 1 (שִׂיחָה / דֶּרֶךְ חָדָשׁ). Package 1 is what bypasses these forces; Package 3 is the force being bypassed.

observations:
Torah #97 (LM2) has zero bechina edges in torahData.js (reference 1097 is absent from the dataset). The teaching is among the shortest in Likutay Moharan Tinyana — four sentences presenting one complete argument through a mashal-nimshal structure.

Despite the absence of explicit 'בְּחִינַת' language, the teaching contains genuine bechina-type identifications:

1. The 'הוּא' (is/equals) identification: 'הַשִּׂיחָה שֶׁמְּדַבֵּר הָאָדָם עַצְמוֹ בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ, הוּא דֶּרֶךְ חָדָשׁ וּתְפִלָּה חֲדָשָׁה' — this is a direct equation of three concepts through shared essential quality (novelty/unknownness to the adversarial forces).

2. The mashal-nimshal structure creates structural bechina pairs: תְּפִלּוֹת הַסְּדוּרוֹת = דֶּרֶךְ הַכְּבוּשָׁה (both are 'known', both are therefore vulnerable); הַמְחַבְּלִים וְהַמְקַטְרְגִים = רוֹצְחִים וְגַזְלָנִים (both 'lie in ambush' on known paths).

Three packages are proposed:
- Package 1 (good): the hitbodedut prayer as new/unknown path — 3 nodes
- Package 2 (neutral): set prayers / beaten road — 2 nodes — the structurally vulnerable middle domain
- Package 3 (evil): accusers and robbers — 2 nodes — the adversarial forces

The good/evil mirror is clear: Package 1 (שִׂיחָה חֲדָשָׁה) is what bypasses Package 3 (הַמְחַבְּלִים). Package 2 is the neutral structural domain that becomes the theater of the conflict.

The eitza flow between packages: Package 2 (set prayers on known paths) →eitza→ Package 3 (accusers lie in ambush) — this is the problem the teaching addresses; Package 1 (hitbodedut) →eitza→ bypasses Package 3 (accusers cannot find the new path) — this is the solution.
